introduction.text: The Columbarium of Pomponius Hylas is a 1st‑century Roman burial structure near Porta Latina in Rome, notable for its early dating, inscriptions, and mosaic decoration that illustrate Roman funerary practices and art.

history.description: The columbarium was constructed between 14 and 54 CE, as indicated by inscriptions dedicated to freedmen of Tiberius and Claudia Octavia.
Pomponius Hylas, who owned the columbarium, lived during the Flavian period (69–96 CE).
The columbarium was discovered and excavated in 1831 by Pietro Campana.

design.description: The columbarium is a Roman burial structure located near Porta Latina on Via di Porta Latina, featuring niches for urns.

art.description: A mosaic panel over the entrance steps, added by Pomponius Hylas, depicts griffins and bears a dedication to Pomponius Hylas and his freedwoman Pomponia Vitalinis.
